Then the Q is how to get back in sync.

@nosilverv adds:
> And no explicit deliberation isn’t the only way to get sync
> Literally do things together, let your bodies communicate, the bandwidth is so much higher

ie what Bezos is saying:
> working together in a close, organic way
↓
1574246523180679169 [2022-09-26] @Malcolm_Ocean 
In order to get people working in close, organic way, afaict you need two kinds of trust.

This uhhh vaguely maps onto the "exit, voice" thing so I'm gonna steal those terms and call them exit trust and voice trust.
↓
1574246525273882625 [2022-09-26] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
Exit Trust is the trust required to grant autonomy to other agents, so they don't have to waste time/effort/attention/sanity asking for permission for things.

https://t.co/6Cm7fqYlLZ
  [Quoting @Malcolm_Ocean: red tape is a kind of dysfunctional we-ness]
↓
1574246527211536384 [2022-09-26] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
Exit Trust creates the outer boundary of the people working together closely & organically.

It's recursive: Group A needs to trust Group B in order for B to have autonomy to work closely & organically, and B needs to trust that A trusts B.
↓
1574246528503291904 [2022-09-26] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
Voice Trust is the trust required for a person or group (with adequate autonomy from the outside world) to internally get the perspectives of its various people or parts in sync and settle on a course of action that will be carried out.
↓
1574246529703071750 [2022-09-26] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
Voice Trust is what maintains the inner health of the group. People need to feel grounded in their own perspectives & knowings in order to be able to really hear and understand others.
↓
1574246530806161408 [2022-09-26] @Malcolm_Ocean 
Exit & Voice Trust apply on different fractal scales, too. Within a small close team, people still need to give each other autonomy as individuals to do their respective jobs (exit). And within a person, we need to learn to listen & integrate our different voices/views.
↓
1574246532248920064 [2022-09-26] @Malcolm_Ocean 
Upwards in scale, an organization comprised of many teams still does need to have adequate voice between those teams, even if Bezos is right that the total volume should be less. And the org needs exit trust—for it & its partners to be not meddling in each other.
↓
1574246533276618752 [2022-09-26] @Malcolm_Ocean 
Anyway! The implications of these two kinds of trust required for healthy teams is that if you're having trouble coordinating closely, either of these might be a leverage point.
↓
1574246534467706881 [2022-09-26] @Malcolm_Ocean 
Bezos, in this frame, was saying it was not enough exit trust. But he doesn't just say "do it"—"FIGURE OUT a way for teams to communicate less"

ie some communication may be required in the meantime, to establish the boundary of where one team's scope ends and the other's begins.

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand centers on RV's 2022 tweet proposing that 'sync' (embodied coordination) eliminates the need for explicit negotiation—conflicting wants are symptoms of misalignment, not root causes. Malcolm Ocean becomes the primary steward, applying this lens across domains: intimate relationships (sex tape conflict), group decision-making (dinner logistics), organizational design (Bezos on communication as dysfunction), and even AI alignment. The arc is constructive rather than dialectical: early skepticism (CXGonzalez, DRMacIver) is metabolized into nuance (trust types, grief work), and the concept evolves from dyadic intimacy to 'collective consciousness' and 'wespace.' High cohesion (Malcolm repeatedly returns to the seed tweet over 3 years) but utility is mixed—provides vocabulary for conflict resolution but lacks operationalization beyond 'do things together, let bodies communicate.'
